the מיתיבי source at 132a.4, reporting R' Elazar ben Azarya

the תניא כוותיה דרבי יוחנן at 132a.22

props.gloss_en: R' Eliezer: circumcision and all its preparations override Shabbat (cited at 131b.18)
the Rabbis dispute R' Eliezer only over the preparations of circumcision [which, for them, do not override Shabbat]
but circumcision itself overrides Shabbat according to all
from where do we know it? Ulla: it is halakha [a received law]; and so said R' Yitzchak: halakha
R' Elazar ben Azarya: if circumcision, which concerns one of a person's limbs, overrides Shabbat, a fortiori saving a life overrides Shabbat
R' Elazar ben Azarya to R' Akiva: Akiva, the barley-sized bone is a halakha and the quarter-log of blood is a kal vachomer -- and one does not derive a kal vachomer from a halakha
R' Yochanan: the verse says 'on the day' (Lev 12:3) -- on the day, even on Shabbat
R' Yochanan: the 'on the day' written of those lacking atonement is needed to teach by day and not by night
R' Yochanan: that circumcision is by day [not night] is derived from 'and he that is eight days old' (Gen 17:12)
Reish Lakish: that [offerings are by day] too is derived from 'on the day He commanded' (Lev 7:38)

though it is derived from 'on the day He commanded', it was needed: one might think that since the Torah had mercy on him to bring [an offering] in poverty, he may bring it at night too -- it teaches us [he may not]
Rav Acha bar Yaakov: the verse says 'eighth' -- the eighth, even on Shabbat
the baraita's first reading: 'on the eighth he shall be circumcised' -- even on Shabbat; and 'its desecrators shall be put to death' (Ex 31:14) concerns other labours, apart from circumcision
or perhaps [the prohibition covers] even circumcision, and 'on the eighth' means except on Shabbat? the verse says 'on the day' -- even on Shabbat
leprosy overrides the [Temple] service, and the service overrides Shabbat -- and circumcision overrides it [leprosy]

schemas.gloss_en: circumcision, which concerns one of a person's limbs, overrides Shabbat; a fortiori saving a life
the quarter-log of blood, by kal vachomer from the barley-sized bone (which is halakha)

restricted_by.gloss_en: ואין דנין קל וחומר מהלכה -- one does not derive a kal vachomer from a halakha

schemas.gloss_en: אתיא אות אות -- 'sign' of circumcision (Gen 17:11) and 'sign' of Shabbat (Ex 31:13)

grounds.gloss_en: אלא מעתה תפילין דכתיב בהו אות לידחי שבת -- if so, tefillin, of which 'sign' is written, should override Shabbat

schemas.gloss_en: אלא אתיא ברית ברית -- 'covenant' of circumcision and 'covenant' of Shabbat (Ex 31:16)

grounds.gloss_en: גדול דכתיב ביה ברית לידחי שבת -- an adult, of whom 'covenant' is written, should override Shabbat

schemas.gloss_en: אלא אתיא דורות דורות -- 'generations' of Shabbat and 'generations' of circumcision

grounds.gloss_en: ציצית דכתיב ביה דורות לידחי שבת -- tzitzit, of which 'generations' is written, should override Shabbat

schemas.gloss_en: דנין אות ברית ודורות מאות ברית ודורות -- לאפוקי הנך דחד חד הוא דכתיב בהן: sign, covenant and generations together, excluding those [tefillin, an adult, tzitzit] of which only one is written
leprosy overrides the service, the service overrides Shabbat, and circumcision overrides leprosy; Shabbat, which yields to the service -- is it not right that circumcision override it?

grounds.gloss_en: וממאי דצרעת חמורה? דילמא שבת חמורה, שכן יש בה עונשין ואזהרות הרבה -- whence that leprosy is the graver? perhaps Shabbat is, with its many punishments and warnings
אי נמי: וממאי משום דחמירא צרעת היא, דילמא משום גברא הוא דלא חזי -- or: whence that [the service yields] because leprosy is grave? perhaps it is because the man is unfit

supports.gloss_en: תניא כוותיה דרבי יוחנן -- the baraita concludes: ת"ל ביום, אפילו בשבת

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי: R' Elazar ben Azarya derives saving life by kal vachomer from circumcision; ואי סלקא דעתך הלכה -- קל וחומר מהלכה מי אתי? and he himself taught that one does not derive a kal vachomer from a halakha (= p_ein_danin_kv_mehalacha)
אלא מעתה מחוסרי כפרה דכתיב בהו ביום, הכי נמי דדחו שבת?! -- if so, those lacking atonement, of whom 'on the day' is written, should override Shabbat

answered_by.gloss_en: ההוא מיבעי ליה ביום ולא בלילה -- that is needed for by day and not by night (= p_kapara_bayom_velo_balayla)

objections.gloss_en: האי נמי מיבעי ליה ביום ולא בלילה -- this one [of circumcision] too is needed for by day and not by night

answered_by.gloss_en: ההוא מבן שמונת ימים נפקא -- that comes from 'he that is eight days old' (= p_mila_bayom_mibenshmonat)

objections.gloss_en: מתקיף לה רבינא: אלא מעתה יהא זר כשר בהן ויהא אונן כשר בהן -- if the Torah's mercy relaxes his offering, a non-priest and an acute mourner should be fit to offer them

answered_by.gloss_en: הא אהדריה קרא -- the verse restored it [to the general rule]

objections.gloss_en: האי שמיני מיבעי ליה למעוטי שביעי -- this 'eighth' is needed to exclude the seventh

answered_by.gloss_en: שביעי מבן שמונת ימים נפקא -- the seventh is excluded by 'he that is eight days old'

objections.gloss_en: ואכתי מיבעי ליה, חד למעוטי שביעי וחד למעוטי תשיעי -- for from one I would say the seventh is excluded as its time has not come, but from the eighth on is its time; אלא מחוורתא כדרבי יוחנן
תניא ... ודלא כרב אחא בר יעקב -- the baraita's tanna sets 'eighth' aside (או אינו) and rests on 'on the day'
